newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SOUTH AFRICA DESERVE FINAL TEST WIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SOUTH AFRICA DESERVE FINAL TEST WIN.

text.p: South Africa salvaged some pride from their series defeat by the British Lions with a deserved 35-16 victory in the third and final test at Ellis Park on Saturday.
Determined to avoid a total whitewash in the three tests, the Springboks outscored the Lions four tries to one as the series finished 2-1 in the tourists' favour.
New cap Jannie de Beer kicked 13 points with three penalties and two conversions while his side controlled the majority of play with some passionate rugby.

The Springbok threequarters displayed a great deal more vision than in the first two tests and scored tries through centre Percy Montgomery, scrumhalf Joost van der Westhuizen and wings Andre Snyman and Pieter Rossouw.

The Lions, whose rock-solid defence was yet again impressive during the first half, replied with an individual try from halfback Matt Dawson and three penalties and a conversion from impressive Welsh fullback Neil Jenkins.
Just as they did in the second test in Durban, the Springbok forwards began the match in ferocious style and managed to exercise a stranglehold on proceedings for most of the first period.
South Africa soon opened up an early 6-0 lead through successive penalties from the 26-year-old flyhalf de Beer.
Although de Beer shaved the right-hand upright with his third penalty attempt in only the 12th minute, the Springboks extended their advantage to 13-0 with a converted try just three minutes later.

A period of sustained possession set up a South African scrum in the Lions' 22. De Beer fed outside centre Percy Montgomery who crossed the line unopposed in the lefthand corner. The outside half then converted.
Yet, on the rare occasions when the Lions entered Springbok territory, the South Africans gave away penalties. The composed Jenkins secured the necessary points for his team.

Offsides by the Springboks in the 19th minute, stamping in the 24th and a loose punch in the 35th provided Jenkins with three penalties in three attempts and narrowed South Africa's lead to 13-9 at the break.
But a sparkling solo try from scrumhalf van der Westhuizen at the start of the second half set the tone after the interval.

The talented halfback peeled off the base of a loose maul, shook off the defence of both Dawson and replacement Allan Bateman and evaded a half-hearted tackle from Jenkins to score by the right corner flag.
De Beer converted from near the touchline to give South Africa a 20-9 lead.
A third de Beer penalty after the Lions were guilty of hands in a ruck put South Africa 23-9 ahead entering the final quarter.

The Lions narrowed the gap with an excellent try from Dawson after he side-stepped his way over the line after breaking away from the back of a maul. Jenkins slotted his fourth kick out of four to bring the score to 23-16.
But, with nine minutes remaining, right wing Rossouw sliced through the Lions' midfield and provided sufficient space in the tackle for left wing Snyman to touch down in the corner.
Rossouw then jinked round three Lions defenders to run in South Africa's fourth try two minutes from the end. Centre replacement Henry Honiball, kicking in place of the injured de Beer, converted.
Teams:

South Africa: 15-Russell Bennett; 14-Andre Snyman, 13-Percy Montgomery (Henry Honiball, 57th), 12-Danie van Schalkwyk, 11-Pieter Rossouw; 10-Janie de Beer (Justin Swart, 73rd), 9-Joost van der Westhuizen (Werner Swanepoel, 83rd), 8-Gary Teichmann (captain) (Fritz van Heerden 74 min), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Johan Erasmus, 5-Krynauw Otto, 4-Hannes Strydom, 3-Dawie Theron, 2-James Dalton (Naka Drotske 71st), 1-Os du Randt (Adrian Garvey 66th, du Randt 83rd).
